text:
marta: opened a tiny PR to fix the embeddings API example in the reference. it currently shows `input` as a string which confuses users about batching. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4802

kevin: good catch. runtime accepts string for backwards compat but docs should show arrays. can you paste the bad snippet?

marta: yep — page currently has:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  \"model\": \"open-embed-1\",
  \"input\": \"hello world\"
}
```
which implies single-item only. proposing this replacement:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  \"model\": \"open-embed-1\",
  \"input\": [\"hello world\", \"search query\"]
}
```
plus a line explaining the response `data` is ordered and corresponds 1:1 to inputs.

docs-bot: lint failure on PR earlier: openapi components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest.example.input must be an array, found string. see CI: https://ci.redwood-inference/1300/logs/998 :warning:

oliver: we should also update the code-snippet generator so it doesn't collapse length-1 arrays to a bare string. there's a legacy template that does that.

emma: i can patch the snippet generator. will change the JS/py templates to always emit arrays for `input`. also will add a unit test asserting the rendered HTML contains \"input\": [\"hello world\"]

kevin: thanks. can you also add a one-paragraph migration note: "SDKs will auto-wrap single-string inputs; for bulk indexing, prefer explicit arrays to avoid subtle performance pitfalls." helps support.

marta: added the migration paragraph in the PR description and included a short python example: `if isinstance(payload['input'], str): payload['input'] = [payload['input']]`. also added a Go snippet with helper wrapIfSingle().

docs-bot: CI re-run: lint passed after example fix, but docs build failed on one flaky image asset. re-run build. https://ci.redwood-inference/1300/builds/104 :arrow_forward:

docs-bot: CI passed (build 105) :white_check_mark: https://ci.redwood-inference/1300/builds/105

oliver: merged. small follow-up: update /docs/migration/embedding-array.md to include a note about `data[].index` being stable and tools that rely on index ordering (e.g., bulk upserts). i'll file a tiny follow-up for that.

emma: filed PR against SDK repo to ensure generators emit arrays for `input` across languages. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/901

sam: support asked that we add a sentence calling out that `data` is always an array even when single input provided. added to migration doc draft.

marta: awesome. thanks all — closing thread. :tada:
